newsitem.title: CHINA: China gold output seen near 130 tonnes in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China gold output seen near 130 tonnes in 1997.

text.p: China is expected to produce nearly 130 tonnes of gold this year, up from just over 120 tonnes in 1996, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Gold output in May was 10.7 tonnes, the newspaper quoted officials of the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry's Gold Bureau as saying.
Total production in the first five months came to 46 tonnes, up 17 percent compared with the same period in 1996, they said.
Banks' willingness to buy gold had fuelled the growth in production, said gold production section official Ai Dacheng.

"Unlike other industries in China that are restricted by the market situation, the gold industry is free of limitations such as an oversupplied market, stockpiles and delayed payment from buyers," the newspaper quoted Ai as saying.
The guaranteed Chinese purchase price for gold was around 91 yuan ($10.96) per gramme, compared with around $347 per ounce on the international market, it said but gave no details.
China has said it plans to raise annual gold output to 150 tonnes by the end of the century.
